top.line: Why we can now connect any data source with any other, owner by owner, with a person in charge.

in-short.line: The disconnect; any data with any data; nine steps; owners keep control; code runs it; a product.

disconnect.line: In Portugal, areas, entities and data sources each hold part of a picture and none sees the whole.
disconnect.para: Joining it is usually years of work.

claim.line: Access, parse, transform, vault, move, key, open, map, output: LETS across a boundary.

why.line: The storm site joined 34 public datasets in a night; PrompTugal.news runs an agent per town.
why.para: A swap is a smaller version.

control.line: No shared platform; encrypted travel; each side chooses the slice; keys per version; all signed.

gates.line: Agents build; a person approves access, every key that crosses, and public outputs; code runs it.
gates.para: Tokens go into building, not running.

examples.line: Weather and schools, water and tourism, heritage and planning, local news and public records.

product.line: Connect two, five, fifty or a hundred datasets, as an agentic cell, on the open stack.

limits.line: Access is the owner's call; examples are proposals; personal data still needs a legal basis.

sources.line: A conversation on 17 November 2026 and earlier articles.
